issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the boolean attribute of ExcellenceLand: the UML in the problem statement declares a boolean attribute named 'excellentEnough' (problem_statement.md line 36), but the solution implementation declares a boolean field named 'isExcellent' and provides a getter isExcellent() (solution src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java line 8). This mismatch can confuse students about which field name and getter to implement (the exercise tests check the constructor and getters for ExcellenceLand), potentially causing failing tests or wrong implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the boolean field and its getter in the implementation from 'isExcellent' / isExcellent() to 'excellentEnough' / isExcellentEnough() and update the constructor parameter name accordingly so they match the UML and the exercise tests; or (B) update the UML/problem statement to declare the boolean attribute as 'isExcellent' (and update examples/tests) if that name is preferred. Ensure the constructor parameter order and getter name in the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use the same identifier.
